Subject: Request: encryption & KMS artifacts for SOC2/SIG review

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call earlier this week. Our SOC2/SIG assessment team is starting the technical evidence collection and has asked for a focused set of artifacts around your encryption and key management controls. Could you provide the following (PDF/CSV/diagram preferred):

- High-level diagram of key custody and trust boundaries (cloud KMS vs. HSM vs. customer-managed keys)
- Description of what keys are used to encrypt customer data at rest vs. envelope keys (where applicable)
- Recent key rotation audit (last 12 months) with timestamps and operator IDs — redactions for personal data are fine
- HSM attestation or summary of FIPS/SOC/HSM provider claims (certs or summary page)
- KMS access control policy (roles that can create/rotate/delete keys) and separation-of-duties description
- Any KMS-related incident tickets in the last 24 months (high level)

We need these artifacts to accept Redwood as an approved vendor in our clinical workloads. Target turnaround for evidence is 5 business days if possible. If there are items that you cannot share, please indicate what alternative evidence or controls you can provide.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
InfoSec Manager, Alpha Health

Hi Priya, Vivek — attaching the initial bundle and a short implementation note.

Attachments (attached to this thread):
- redwood_kms_key_lifecycle_diagram.png (high-level custody boundaries and flow)
- rotation_log_redacted_2025-11.csv (pseudonymized operator IDs, UTC timestamps)
- hsm_attestation_summary_v1.pdf (attestation summary from our HSM provider, redacted contact details)

Implementation note (summary):
- Envelope encryption: each tenant has a unique data encryption key (DEK). DEKs are generated by the KMS and encrypted with a customer-tenant master key (TMK) that is HSM-protected.
- TMKs are stored in our HSM provider with hardware-backed key material; we do not store plain key material outside the HSM.
- Rotation cadence: TMKs are rotated on a 12-month schedule by default; DEKs rotate on tenant-triggered key refresh or when a rekey job runs (schedules vary by workload).
- Access controls: KMS admin role (two-person approval for destructive ops) + crypto-ops role for rotation jobs + read-only audit role for compliance. All administrative actions are logged to an immutable audit stream with retention of 3 years.
- Incident history: no KMS compromise incidents in the last 24 months; two operational tickets related to key provisioning latency (tickets redacted).

If you want the CSV exported with different columns or additional filtering (e.g., rotation events only), tell us which columns you need and we can produce it within the 5-business-day window.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Head of Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference

Priya / team — quick technical clarifications from crypto ops to expedite your assessment: 

- The rotation_log_redacted_2025-11.csv includes fields: event_id, key_id (aliased), event_type (rotate/create/deprecate), timestamp_utc, operator_alias, change_request_id. We removed stack traces and internal ticket bodies for confidentiality.
- For HSM attestation: the attached summary lists FIPS 140-2/3 level and the provider's audit cadence. If Alpha Health requires the full HSM vendor report for SOC audit review, we can arrange an NDA/update with the vendor and provide a reviewer copy under the vendor's disclosure policy — that process typically takes 3–5 business days.
- Access policy: destructive KMS operations (e.g., key deletion, export) require two independent approvers and an automated delay window; export of raw key material from HSM is disabled by default and only permissible under strict emergency procedures documented in our runbook.

Laura — can you confirm whether legal should send the vendor NDA or if we should route through procurement? Once confirmed we'll start the vendor disclosure flow.

-Rishi
